subject: Pilot flexibility: termination buffer & phased onboarding ask (Lumera)
messages:
From: Andrew Lewis <andrew.lewis@lumerahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot flexibility: termination buffer & phased onboarding ask (Lumera)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with throughput and the billing clarity. Before we move to signature the procurement team raised two items we need to resolve:

1) Early termination exposure: Our finance team is asking for an explicit 30-day opt-out during the initial pilot window with a proportional rebate on committed credits. They want to avoid a full-term penalty if the pilot doesn't meet clinical throughput expectations.

2) Phased ramp schedule: We proposed a staggered ramp in the SOW (25% first 30 days, 50% next 30 days, full commit thereafter). Procurement wants a softer ramp with an initial 60-day low-volume period and an ability to pause escalation if utilization lags.

I attached our redlines (Lumera_Redlines_v1.pdf). Can you escalate to your deal desk / leadership and confirm what concessions are possible without opening broader precedent risks? We are hopeful a limited concession here will keep this moving to signature this month.

Appreciate it —
Andrew Lewis
Director, Procurement
Lumera Health

--

Subject: Fwd: Pilot flexibility: termination buffer & phased onboarding ask (Lumera)

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Lumera's procurement note. High priority: they want a 30-day opt-out in pilot + softer ramp cadence. They attached redlines.

Context / ask: Lumera is a high-prob net-new healthcare account (pilot -> potential Dedicated next year). My read: we can tolerate a constrained concession if we limit precedent and require clear triggers + notice. Proposed deal terms to consider for approval:
- 30-day opt-out limited to first 90 days of pilot only (one-off right)
- Prorated credit for unused committed tokens during any opt-out window (cap to onboarding credit amount)
- Staged ramp to 60/90/180 with a mandatory utilization review at day 60; if utilization < threshold, we roll to fallback pricing rather than immediate termination.
- One-time onboarding credit (not recurring) to offset early churn risk; suggest $50k credit.

Marissa — can you review contract implications (redlines attached) and confirm whether legal/finance need to sign off before exec indicates approval? Karthik — would you support a limited concession like above or push back for stricter ramp milestones?

Thanks —
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot flexibility: termination buffer & phased onboarding ask (Lumera)

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary. I read the redlines. Quick stance from me: we should approve a narrow, timeboxed concession that protects revenue and precedent. Approve the following with conditions:

- 30-day opt-out: allowed only within the first 90 days of the pilot, one-time right. Customer must provide 30 days' written notice and cite unmet KPIs.
- Proration rule: any refund/credit equals the unused portion of committed credits in the remainder of the pilot period, capped at the one-time onboarding credit ($50,000). No recurring refunds.
- Phased ramp: replace proposed 25/50/full with a 60/90/180 cadence. Insert utilization review at day 60 with quantitative thresholds (tokens/day or latency SLAs). If thresholds not met, move customer to fallback per-token pricing instead of cancelling immediately.
- Legal to bless the opt-out clause language; Finance to confirm accounting for onboarding credit and credit cap.

Marissa — please prepare the redline that captures the opt-out window language and the proration formula. Also add a clause that blocks Lumera from invoking the opt-out more than once across consecutive engagements.

If legal/finance are comfortable, I authorize Sofia to communicate this as our final concession. No additional discounting beyond the one-time credit.

Karthik
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.com>, Finance <finance@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot flexibility: termination buffer & phased onboarding ask (Lumera)

Karthik / Sofia — attaching a concise redline snippet for the contract (see attachments). Key bullets implemented in redline:
- Defined "Pilot Period" and single-use "Pilot Opt-Out" that terminates service effective 30 days after customer notice.
- Proration: calculation = (CommittedCredits - ConsumedCredits) * (RemainingDays / TotalPilotDays), capped at $50,000.
- Utilization Review: defined metric = average tokens/day over a 7-day window at day 60; threshold set at 70% of agreed baseline. Failure moves customer to fallback per-token rate for remaining term.
- Clause preventing reuse of opt-out in future commercial agreements without executive waiver.

Next steps: Legal to confirm final clause wording (I flagged a sentence about \"no material share of audit logs\" — legal please review), Finance to confirm the credit treatment (revenue recognition / reserve). If both sign off, Karthik's approval stands and Sofia can communicate to Lumera and upload the signed amendment to DocuSign.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-14T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot flexibility: termination buffer & phased onboarding ask (Lumera)

Andrew — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. Good news: leadership approved a narrowly scoped concession. Summary of the approved approach (final, subject to legal/finance sign-off and amendment):

1) Pilot Opt-Out: Lumera may exercise a one-time 30-day opt-out during the first 90 days of the pilot. Notice must be in writing.
2) Proration & Credit Cap: Any credit due will be prorated per the contract formula and capped at a one-time onboarding credit of $50,000.
3) Phased Onboarding: Pilot cadence set to 60/90/180 days with a utilization review at day 60. If utilization falls below the agreed metric, customer will be moved to the fallback per-token pricing for the remainder of the term (rather than immediate contract termination).
4) No broader precedent: Opt-out is single-use and cannot be invoked in future renewals without exec waiver.

Please review and tell me if Lumera is comfortable with the cap and the utilization-review fallback. If yes, we'll issue a short amendment and route via DocuSign (link will follow). Legal and Finance are looped on our side for final sign-off.

Next step: I'll send a draft amendment by tomorrow and include the DocuSign link once legal confirms final wording.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
